en: Warp drive disengaged.\nWe will soon be arriving in\ntarget planet's orbit.
Compared to our landing\nin Maere, this was a walk\nin the park!
Operating a ship without\nshields...
...was akin to calculating pi\nwith no memory.

I haven't the slightest clue
what you're on about, but
the important thing is that
we landed safely!

Yes, but that is not to say
we can rest easy! We
must find spare parts and
materials with which to
repair our ship posthaste!
In that case, I hereby\nbestow upon this planet\nthe name <font color=yellow>Esperance</font>...
...in hopes that this planet\nwill provide us with all that\nwe need!

I shall register that name
in my systems. Let us
pray that this place lives
up to your expectations!

Ah, Captain, if I may! First
things first―we must
check the atmosphere of
this planet.

I detect a large group of
man-made structures
indicative of a
metropolitan area. The
people here have reached
a higher level of
civilization than those on
Maere.
In addition to that there\nare...
...D-dear maker!
There appears to be a\nlarge cavern just beneath\nthe planet's surface!
A large underground\ncavern!?

With the limited
information at my disposal,
I am unable to determine
if the civilization here is
technologically capable of
creating something such
as this.

I have a hunch, however,
the answer is "no." If I
were to hazard a guess, I
might even say someone
is siphoning their
resources.

And before you ask, yes,
AI can have hunches! That
feature has been built into
my programming.
M-my apologies, Captain!\nAllow me to clarify.

Only civilizations that have
reached a certain level of
sophistication would be
able to create the cavern
I am seeing.

If I had to generate an
estimate, I would say
there is a 50 percent
chance that the people
here have excavated it
themselves.
Do you think we should\nmove on?
No. Let's land. I want to\nget to the bottom of this.
We have no choice but to\nland―we need materials.
I'll let you decide!

Captain, you are
possessed of a heart of
gold! If I had anything
resembling tear ducts, I
would be crying streams
of oil!
I am overjoyed to hear\nthat you are on the same\npage as I am!

We cannot stand idly by
and watch as a planet's
resources are exploited
for some nefarious
purpose!
Your wish is my command!
Your judgment is sound,\nCaptain. I fully support\nyour decision.

And if, as we suspect, the
people of this planet are
being deprived of their
resources, together we
shall bring the hammer of
justice down upon the
perpetrators!
M-me!?
My programming bars me\nfrom making decisions in\nplace of my ship's captain.
I, however, anticipated\nthat such a day would\ncome and prepared this...

Behold─the die! This is a
time-tested device from
the days of yore used to
generate a random
outcome.

Should it land on a side
with an odd number, we
shall descend. If we roll an
even number, we leave
this place.

Enough of this nonsense!
If the two of you can't
decide, then I will! We are
landing!
...To think I prepared that\ndie for nothing...
Captain, are you fine with\nthis decision?
Then I shall commence our\nlanding sequence.

I am afraid to report that,
as soon as we entered
the planet's atmosphere,
the short-range sensors
quit responding.
It seems our suspicions\nmay have been correct...

Are the waves jamming
our signals the exact
same as those we
encountered on Maere?
Yes, but there is more.
Hmph! ...What now?
Before our sensors went\ndown, I got a quick glance\nof the nearby city.

The number of life-forms
occupying it is
disproportionately small
compared to the scale of
the metropolis.
So a large portion of the\nlocals are missing?

Actually, it is quite a bit
worse than that... A more
accurate way to describe
this phenomenon is to say
that their population is on
the verge of extinction.

I think the best course of
action would be to leave
this place and head for
the next star system.

Where there are jamming
signals, there is a tower!
We must find and
dismantle it!
Ensuring your safety and\nprotecting the ship are my\nmain functions.
As such, I must insist that\nwe leave...
We cannot turn a blind\neye to what is happening\nhere!
<player>, do you remember\nhow we first met?
You saved me―a virtual\nstranger―from a terrible\nfate!

Were it not for you, I
would be dead. I cannot
tell you how thankful I am
for you rescuing me that
day.
Eve... You are a lot more\nsensitive than you seem...
Eek!
Moving on...
I know how it is to feel\nhopeless. I simply cannot\nabandon these people...

Captain, if it is your wish, I
have no choice but to
comply! Launching
investigation sequence.
You are so easily swayed...

I suggest we begin by
surveying the city grounds
to determine what could
have caused this
reduction in the local
population.

Eve, take this―a
counter-jammer―and see
that it is set up properly.
We need to bring our
sensors back online.
Godspeed, the two of you!\nCome back safe!
Excellent! You have made\nit to the survey point.
This is the former city. It\nhas been overrun by\nvegetation.

Judging from the sheer
volume of overgrowth, it
looks like it has been
abandoned for a while...
How did this happen...?

If I had to guess, some
sort of calamity caused
the ecosystem to collapse,
resulting in what you see
before you.
I cannot offer you much\nmore of an explanation\nthan that.
Yes! Yes, indeed! Brilliant\nidea, Captain!

If we were to run some
lab work on the plantlike
creature you battled
earlier, that might give us
a clue!
I will bring back a sample\nfor you, then.
Understood! I shall be\nwaiting to receive it, arms\nopen wide!

Giant! Massive! Colossal!
What are you on about\nnow?

We are in huge trouble. A
large wall obstructs our
search forward, and I fear
our only solution is to
retreat!

Please, do not be angry
with me... I know you do
not want to hear it, but it
is our only choice...

Oh, no! I see it
coming―you are going to
erupt in anger! I must run
away! Escape to a safe
place, where I will stay for
days―maybe weeks―until
your ire fades...
Calm yourself!
Captain, I apologize for\nthe fuss.

The route along which you
must continue your
investigation has been
blocked off by an
enormous wall.
Should you wish to press\nforward, you must first\nfind a way to scale it.
How troubling... And there\nare no alternate routes we\ncan take, I presume?

No feasible ones, anyway.
The rest of the
surrounding areas are all
cliffs...
Hmmm, maybe we should\ngo and have a look.
Up close it may not be\nnearly as daunting.
That should be the last of\nthem.
...Done.
...Wait! I sense the\nmovements of a larger\nplant-based life-form!
Over there.

It is humongous! Perhaps
the wall was not at all a
wall, but this hulking
beast!
About that I have no\ndoubts.

Considering the size of
that thing, I do not think it
wise to proceed with this
operation. You need to
retreat.
Normally I'd agree.

I, however, have found
something that will allow
us to prevail against these
long odds.
And what might that be?
Look there.
A...detour!?
While everyone was busy\nfighting, I did a bit of\nreconnaissance.

It is difficult to spy from a
distance because the
opening is hidden in the
tree's roots.
I suspect this tunnel was\nonce used as an\nexpressway.
How wonderful! Perhaps\nthere is still hope for this\nmission to succeed!
I'd certainly say so.
You have started to\nfinally pull your own weight\naround here, Eve!

I am just joking! Pulling
your leg! Making a
wisecrack! Please do not
take me so seriously.
...I shall behave myself.\nAhem. Now then, let us\ncontinue forging ahead!
I will run an analysis on\nyour current location.
...You'll pay for what you\nsaid when I get back.

Update! I have detected
the corpses of numerous
plant-based life-forms up
ahead!
Corpses?

Perhaps it is a graveyard
of some kind--a place
where these creatures
travel when they feel
death is upon them?

Considering they all have
external wounds, I would
sooner conclude they
were killed by someone...or
something.
Who, or what, would do\nsuch a thing...?
I do not know.

Excellent theory, Captain! I
agree that this could be
the doing of the local
citizens. They rose up to
fight off these creatures!
The people are in distress!\nWe must do our utmost to\nsave them!
Yes, but all we have to go\non so far are mere\nspeculations.

We know not the dangers
that await us. ...Captain,
what do you suggest we
do?
As Eve says, we must\nrush to the locals' aid.
It is too late to turn back.\nThe only way is forward.
Pack me some bananas. I\nneed a snack for the road.
That you should disregard\nyour own safety in favor\nof helping those in need...

This is altruism at its
finest--a sentiment AI will
never be able to
understand! I so dearly
admire you for it, Captain!

Your steadfast devotion
to <player> is not so
dissimilar to the spirit of
altruism, Coro.
You do not sound\nparticularly enthusiastic\nabout this...

I beg to differ. In fact, I
would say the captain is
extremely excited, just too
shy to show it!

But of course! I have, in
fact, researched a number
of different ways I can
prepare bananas for
precisely such an
occasion!

We have banana omelets,
stewed bananas, and a
banana saute with
hollandaise sauce.
Take your pick!
We are embarking upon a\nscouting mission, not a\npicnic!

Come on, Captain! Let us
go before Coro's mindless
antics cause us to forget
our priorities!
Are you all right!?

Just barely. I have the
captain and our allies to
thank... They managed to
keep the worst at bay.

It seems our earlier
assumption about the
corpses being the result
of a local uprising was
incorrect.
Instead, these life-forms\nare the ones to blame.
We are no strangers to\nthese creatures.
Their hulking shape, their\nunique fighting style...
...but most of all their\nglowing spikes―there is no\nmistaking them.

I will run a more in-depth
analysis later, but a
preliminary scan suggests
you are not wrong.
Primitive life-forms with\nthorns as their defining\nfeature...
Henceforth, we shall call\nthem <font color=yellow>Thornites</font>.

I wonder what exactly
they are...and if they are
somehow associated with
the men who built these
towers...
*Sigh* ...Never mind.

To attempt to draw
conclusions using
insufficient evidence will
get us nowhere. Let's
instead turn our attention
to our next task.

Before you go, please
secure a sample from the
beast that I might study it
upon your return.
Finally! At long last! After\nall this time!

I have managed to track
down the location of the
tower emitting jamming
signals!
Took you long enough.

If the one here on
Esperance is anything like
the structure we
encountered on Maere,
our first order of business
would be to remove its
source of power.
...Esperance...? Mae...re...?\nWho are they?

Esperance is the name of
the planet we are
currently on and Maere is
the planet we just came
from!
What is wrong with you?\nHas your memory\nshort-circuited!?

Ah, yes! I remember now! I
forgot to register those
names in my memory
bank.
You better not have\nforgotten to register mine.
Er...about that...
Aaaaaah!
Eve, I am jesting! Poking\nfun! Joking!
Please, direct your\npunches at the tower and\nnot me!

I was not aware robots
could tell lies. The next
time you pull a trick like
this, I shall soak your
console in salt water!

Let's leave now, Captain!
My blood is boiling with
rage and I need something
to take it out on!
Fantastic work. I have\nconfirmed that the tower\nis down.
Our short-range sensors\nare back up and running.
Thank heavens! This will\nmake our lives a lot\neasier.
Good thing we were clever\nenough to outwit whoever\nbuilt these towers!
Before you return, please\nbe sure to recover the\nenergy unit.
Consider it done.

You will be pleased to
hear that the results from
the samples you took off
those plantlike creatures
have come back!

What they reveal is simply
incredible! Not even in my
wildest dreams could I
have―
Hurry up and tell us\nalready.

Just as the finest wines
take decades to develop
their rich flavors, great
discoveries grow all the
sweeter with anticipa―

You brought that upon
yourself! If you had simply
told us what we needed to
know, the captain wouldn't
have had to reboot you!

M-my apologies! Long
story short, I have
determined what has
caused Esperance's
ecosystem to collapse.

Good work, Coro. Now
continue, lest I beat your
habit of rambling out of
you...
Not worth your while?\nThis is likely the most\nimportant― Ahem. Sorry.

You see, the DNA of the
creatures you brought
back to me are all perfect
matches.

This means, that while it
appears you are fighting
many different enemies, in
actuality they are all one
organism.
What do you mean?
Simply put, they are all\nclones of the same\nself-replicating life-form.

So this organism is cloning
itself in a process similar
to how primitive forms of
plankton reproduce?
Exactly. The only\ndifference being...

The DNA of this creature
is far more complex than
that of plankton and
replicating said structure
is far more difficult.

This means that
replication errors will
occur at a much higher
rate. Most creatures that
attempt this would die.
So how does it keep\ncloning itself? There are\nso many of them!
Exactly right, Captain!\nThere is a source!
...Something like what\nmaster data is to\ncomputer data. An original.

If it were to perish, these
creatures would no longer
continue to come into
existence.
I see...

Seeing as the sensors are
back up, we can use them
to track down the parent
creature.
I will inform you as soon\nas I find it.
Here, right?
Yes. The parent creature\nshould be somewhere\nnearby.
...What do you think could\nhave caused such a tragic\nfate to befall this planet?

Judging from the state of
their metropolis, this
disaster seems to be a
more recent occurrence.

An external factor likely
sent this creature's
replication functions into
overdrive.

The local citizens, having
no way to foresee such an
event, were nearly wiped
out by this disaster.
An external factor...?

It is just as you say,
Captain! Now is not the
time for speculation―it is
the time for action!
Yes! Precisely right!
Come now! We have a\ncreature to kill and a\nplanet to save!
You did it! My sensors no\nlonger register the\ncreature's presence.

Hurrah! The people of this
planet no longer need to
fear this creature or its
clones.

Now that everything has
been taken care of, it is
time you returned to the
ship.
We are now back in orbit.

Ever since you put down
the parent beast,
Esperance has seen no
more issues with abnormal
replication.
That is a relief.

While their population has
been significantly
diminished, given time I
believe they will recover.
People are resilient. We\nneed not worry about\nthem.
What I would like to know\nis how this happened in\nthe first place...
I have no doubt that the\nmen who built the tower\nare somehow responsible!
There is a good chance\nyou are right.

To think that, in addition
to robbing resources, they
would subject countless
innocent men and women
to such horrors!
We must find and\nincarcerate the\nperpetrators!
Let's do everything in our\npower to help the victims!
Well, I'll be darned―this\nhas turned into a game of\ntag with evildoers!

An excellent idea! We
must find a way to
apprehend them no
matter what!

Considering how vast the
universe is, however, doing
so will by no means be an
easy task.

Regardless, we must
remain steadfast in our
intentions and find a way
to prevail!
Giving up from the get-go\nis no way to produce the\nresults we want.

This was not a civil
dispute―a civilization was
exerting their power over
another planet and their
people!

As a part of the
federation, it is our duty
to see that
underdeveloped planets
such as Esperance are
protected!

Only we must do so
discreetly. We cannot
allow them to become
aware of our presence.

Should our actions be
classified as
"interference," it will be
considered a breach of
the UP3.

While that is an admittedly
odd way of saying you
intend to stop the culprits,
our course of action
remains the same.

Odd phrasing? I disagree!
That is a complete
misappropriation of the
word "tag"!

Tag is a game wherein one
party chases the others in
an effort to touch one of
them.

The more suitable term
would be "hide- and-seek,"
wherein one party hides
while the other attempts
to find them.
...For Pete's sake, no one\ncares! Absolutely no one\ncares!

...I have finally finished
calculating the
coordinates of our next
destination. Let us
continue making for Earth.

If―and when―we come
across the perpetrators
we shall see that they are
permanently struck down!

You have discovered a
New Route. You can now
choose this New Route
from the Select Planet
screen.
